about: Measured apparent-colour response of every Low/Medium and classic High hair path (colour model spec revision 3, 4.4): the lit mean of the hair alone (linear light) on the RL head stage's neutral look, Forward+, front view, 512 px, at tone-mapping exposure 0.50 (unclipped), as a function of the dye d (linear). Keys <sex>/<path>/<style>/<s>: P1 Low/Medium Classic; P2 Classic with length or volume off 50, which is P1's response; P3 Low/Medium at finish position s (0, 25, 75 and 100, and the custom positions 12, 37, 49, 51, 63 and 88 between them; s 50 is P1's response), P4 the classic High hair finish (pigment model) at the same positions and 50; a position in between is linear between its measured neighbours; B1/B2 the Low/Medium and High beard shells by facial_hair. Linear entries: mu = gain * d + floor; pigment entries: see AppearanceColours.model_mu. The apparent colour of dye d is (mu(d) - floor) / skinGain. `shapes` scales a hairstyle's response by its hair length and volume: keys <sex>/<medium|high>/<style>/<s>, measured on a 5 x 5 grid at Classic (s 50) and a 3 x 3 grid at 0, 25, 75 and 100 (Medium for P1-P3, classic High for P4), bilinear, linear in s. Low draws the Medium response: its hair is 1.25-1.65 times brighter than Medium for every colour, palette included, because Low actors cast no shadows (no self-shadowing in the hair); custom colours keep the palette's relationship. Written by tools/colour_calibration/fit_hair.py from tests/integration/hair_apparent_calibration.gd; each entry lists its source files, whose SHA-256 is in `sources` (tests/test_appearance_colours.gd fails when one changes: re-run the probe).
